questions.question:
In a classroom test, students were awarded +6 marks for each correct answer and -3 marks for each incorrect answer. No marks were given for unattempted questions.

Radhika answered 10 questions correctly and scored a total of 42 marks. How many questions did she answer incorrectly?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Marks from 10 correct answers = 10 × 6 = 60

Difference between expected and actual score = 60 − 42 = 18

Each incorrect answer reduces the score by 3 marks.

Number of incorrect answers = 18 ÷ 3 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marks for each correct answer = +6

Marks for each incorrect answer = −3

Number of correct answers = 10

Total marks obtained = 42

**Formula Used:**

Total Score = (Correct answers × Marks per correct) + (Incorrect answers × Marks per incorrect)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e317aa441e48838d73cf6ca4028420adf7b8eb28fecf161fa3351d07adced617.png] 

⇒ Total marks from correct answers = 10 × 6 = 60

⇒ Let the number of incorrect answers be n.

⇒ Total Score = 60 + (n × (−3))

⇒ 42 = 60 − 3n

⇒ 3n = 60 − 42

⇒ 3n = 18

⇒ n = 18 ÷ 3

⇒ n = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Negative Marking System

It is used in competitive exams to penalize wrong guesses. The net score is calculated as: (Correct × Marks) − (Incorrect × Penalty).

Accuracy vs. Attempts

High attempts with low accuracy can result in a lower score than low attempts with 100% accuracy due to negative marking.

Linear Equation in One Variable

Problems involving scores and counts are typically solved using the basic linear form ax + b = c, where x represents the unknown quantity.</p

questions.question: A hollow hemisphere has an inner radius of 5 cm and an outer radius of 7 cm. Find its total surface area.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a hollow hemisphere = π(3R² + r²)

Given: Outer radius (R) = 7 cm, Inner radius (r) = 5 cm

TSA = (22/7) × (3 × 7² + 5²) = (22/7) × (147 + 25)

TSA = (22/7) × 172 ≈ 540.57 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 540.57 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Inner radius (r) = 5 cm

Outer radius (R) = 7 cm

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area = Outer CSA + Inner CSA + Area of Base Ring

TSA = 2πR² + 2πr² + π(R² − r²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/617e741ca60242cea7ab80f862a920193c023bd4e95604f8270b7274db0ffd3e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Outer Curved Surface Area = 2 × (22/7) × 7² = 2 × 22 × 7 = 308 cm²

⇒ Inner Curved Surface Area = 2 × (22/7) × 5² = 1100/7 ≈ 157.14 cm²

⇒ Area of base ring = π(R² − r²) = (22/7) × (49 − 25) = (22/7) × 24 ≈ 75.43 cm²

⇒ Total Surface Area = 308 + 157.14 + 75.43

⇒ Total Surface Area = 540.57 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 540.57 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of Hollow Hemisphere

The volume of a hollow hemisphere is the difference between the volumes of the outer and inner hemispheres: V = 2/3 π(R³ − r³).

Total Surface Area of Solid Hemisphere

For a solid hemisphere of radius r, the total surface area includes the curved surface and the flat circular base: TSA = 3πr².

Curved Surface Area of Hemisphere

The curved surface area (CSA) of any hemisphere is exactly half the surface area of a full sphere: CSA = 2πr².</p

questions.question: What does each point on a number line represent?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

A number line is a continuous geometric representation of all possible values.

Natural numbers and Integers are discrete points with empty spaces between them.

Rational numbers are dense but still leave gaps where irrational numbers exist.

Only the set of Real numbers covers every single point on the line without any gaps.

**∴ The correct answer is Real number.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A point on a number line.

**Formula Used:** Completeness property of the real number system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a97095b458bedb0b0e260aea9a2365acd54785bb98ba4874b41cebbf906f518.png] 

⇒ Natural numbers (N) = {1, 2, 3, ...} → Only specific positive points.

⇒ Integers (Z) = {..., −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, ...} → Only specific whole points.

⇒ Rational numbers (Q) = {p/q | p, q are integers, q ≠ 0} → Excludes values like √2.

⇒ Real numbers (R) = Rational numbers ∪ Irrational numbers.

⇒ There is a one-to-one correspondence between points on the line and real numbers.

**∴ The correct answer is Real number.**

**__Additional Information__**

Completeness Axiom

The real number system is complete, meaning there are no gaps on the number line; every point corresponds to a unique real number.

Density Property

Between any two distinct real numbers, there are infinitely many other real numbers, including both rational and irrational values.

Irrational Numbers

Numbers like √2, √3, and π cannot be expressed as simple fractions and are essential to fill the gaps between rational numbers on the line.</p

questions.question: Find the square of 19.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

To find the square of 19, use the base 20 method.

19 is 1 less than 20. Square of 20 is 400.

19² = (20 − 1)² = 400 − 40 + 1 = 361.

**∴ The correct answer is 361.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number = 19

**Formula Used:**

Square of n = n × n

questions.question: Which of the following is the CORRECT comparison?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Convert all **fractions** to **decimals** for quick comparison.

3/4 = 0.75 | 1/3 ≈ 0.33 | 5/6 ≈ 0.83 | 1/2 = 0.5

Option 1: 0.75 > 0.85 (False)

Option 2: 0.5 0.8 (True)

Option 4: 0.25 > 0.5 (False)

**∴ The correct answer is 5/6 > 0.8.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Comparisons between **fractions** (3/4, 1/3, 5/6, 1/2) and **decimals** (0.85, 0.5, 0.8, 0.25).

**Formula Used:** Decimal Value = Numerator ÷ Denominator

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61a99f621ee4388600a903f59d4aa54984c6124b5a0e6bdc9b9689954215b1fb.png] 

⇒ **Option 1:** 3/4 = 0.75. Since 0.75 0.85 is **incorrect**.

⇒ **Option 2:** 1/3 = 0.333... Since 0.5 > 0.333, the comparison 0.5 0.8, the comparison 5/6 > 0.8 is **correct**.

⇒ **Option 4:** 1/2 = 0.5. Since 0.25 1/2 is **incorrect**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5/6 > 0.8.**

**__Additional Information__**

Comparing Fractions by Cross-Multiplication

To compare a/b and c/d, check the product ad and bc. If ad > bc, then a/b > c/d.

Recurring Decimals

Fractions like 1/3 (0.33...) and 5/6 (0.833...) result in **non-terminating recurring decimals**.

Proper vs Improper Fractions

A **proper fraction** (numerator < denominator) is always less than 1, while an **improper fraction** is 1 or greater.</p

questions.question: The average weight of 10 parcels is 1.5 kg. If a parcel weighing 2.5 kg is replaced by a new parcel, the average weight becomes 1.6 kg. What is the weight of the new parcel?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

New Weight = Old Weight + (Total Count × Change in Average)

Change in Average = 1.6 − 1.5 = 0.1 kg

New Weight = 2.5 + (10 × 0.1)

New Weight = 2.5 + 1.0 = 3.5 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 3.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of parcels = 10

Initial average weight = 1.5 kg

Weight of replaced parcel = 2.5 kg

New average weight = 1.6 kg

**Formula:** Total Weight = Average × Number of items

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0e84e407cb4ba627f811b94f40858bf4b8da06cb4efd39cbed2064969675482e.png] 

⇒ Initial total weight of 10 parcels = 10 × 1.5 = 15 kg

⇒ New total weight of 10 parcels = 10 × 1.6 = 16 kg

⇒ Increase in total weight = 16 − 15 = 1 kg

⇒ This increase is due to the difference between the new and old parcel.

⇒ Weight of new parcel = Weight of old parcel + Increase in total weight

⇒ Weight of new parcel = 2.5 + 1 = 3.5 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 3.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Replacement Rule

When one item is replaced, the value of the new item = Replaced item value + (Total number of items × Increase in average). If the average decreases, the change is taken as negative.

Average Inclusion/Exclusion

When a new item is added to a group, the value of the new item = New Total Sum − Old Total Sum = (n+1) × New Average − n × Old Average.

Weighted Average

The combined average of two groups with counts n₁, n₂ and averages A₁, A₂ is given by (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

questions.question:
A cricketer has an average of 30 runs in 9 innings. In the 10th inning, he scores some runs, and his average increases to 31 runs.

How many runs did he score in the 10th inning?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Runs in 10th inning = New Average + (Previous Innings × Increase in Average)

Increase in average = 31 − 30 = 1

Runs in 10th inning = 31 + (9 × 1)

Runs in 10th inning = 31 + 9 = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average of 9 innings = 30 runs

Average of 10 innings = 31 runs

**Formula Used:**

Total Runs = Average × Number of Innings

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea77389d4af129ab3e2b634ffd198fea5f6bbb55efde0b2849789ded442fa48c.png] 

⇒ Total runs in 9 innings = 9 × 30 = 270

⇒ Total runs in 10 innings = 10 × 31 = 310

⇒ Runs in 10th inning = Total runs in 10 innings − Total runs in 9 innings

⇒ Runs in 10th inning = 310 − 270 = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Concept

The average is the central value of a set of data, calculated as Sum ÷ Count.

Net Deviation Rule

The sum of deviations from the average is always zero. If the average increases by 1 for 10 items, the new item must be (10 × 1) more than the old average.

Weighted Average

When two groups with different averages are combined, the new average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: A student got 30% marks and failed by 13 marks and another student got 44% marks and gets 15 more than the passing marks. Find the maximum mark in a certain examination?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Difference in percentage = 44% − 30% = 14%

Total difference in marks = 13 (fail) + 15 (pass) = 28

14% of Maximum Marks = 28

1% of Maximum Marks = 2

100% of Maximum Marks = 2 × 100 = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Student 1: Marks = 30%, Status = Failed by 13 marks

Student 2: Marks = 44%, Status = Passed by 15 marks

**Formula Used:**

Passing Marks = (Marks obtained) + (Failing marks) = (Marks obtained) − (Excess marks)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/526c487b030280e0d9fbe50356a01324e6447394bf3dbee4af929d22b1180e3a.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the maximum marks be x.

⇒ Passing Marks = 30% of x + 13

⇒ Passing Marks = 44% of x − 15

⇒ 30% of x + 13 = 44% of x − 15

⇒ 13 + 15 = 44% of x − 30% of x

⇒ 28 = 14% of x

⇒ 28 = (14 ÷ 100) × x

⇒ x = (28 × 100) ÷ 14

⇒ x = 2 × 100

⇒ x = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200.**

**__Additional Information__**

Passing Percentage

To find the passing percentage, calculate (Passing Marks ÷ Maximum Marks) × 100. In this case: (30% of 200 + 13) = 60 + 13 = 73. Passing % = (73 ÷ 200) × 100 = 36.5%.

Percentage Change

Percentage change = (Difference ÷ Original Value) × 100. This is useful for comparing marks between different exams or students.

Base Change Rule

If a student's marks increase by a% and then decrease by a%, the net change is always a decrease of (a² ÷ 100)%.</p

questions.question: A student scored 14.75 out of 20 in Science and 17 1/2 out of 25 in Maths. In which subject did she score better percentage-wise?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Science score: 14.75/20 → Scale to 100 by multiplying by 5 ⇒ 14.75 × 5 = 73.75%.

Maths score: 17.5/25 → Scale to 100 by multiplying by 4 ⇒ 17.5 × 4 = 70%.

Comparing the results: 73.75% > 70%.

The student performed better in Science.

**∴ The correct answer is Science.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Science score = 14.75 out of 20

Maths score = 17 1/2 out of 25 = 17.5 out of 25

**Formula Used:**

Percentage = (Marks Obtained ÷ Total Marks) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9a04b7c234b532a900e3deca203e8f42ef3c376bfb1a8809907f5e0ad27b8aa8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Science Percentage = (14.75 ÷ 20) × 100

⇒ Science Percentage = 14.75 × 5 = 73.75%

⇒ Maths Percentage = (17.5 ÷ 25) × 100

⇒ Maths Percentage = 17.5 × 4 = 70%

⇒ Since 73.75% > 70%, the Science score is better.

**∴ The correct answer is Science.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage Calculation

To find the percentage of a value, use: (Part ÷ Whole) × 100. This standardizes different totals for easy comparison.

Comparing Fractions

Fractions can be compared by converting them to decimals or by making their denominators equal (like converting both to a base of 100).

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

To convert a fraction to a percentage, multiply the fraction by 100 and add the % symbol. Example: 3/4 × 100 = 75%.</p

questions.question: A seller buys 240 Television. He sells some of them at a gain of 20% and the remaining at a gain of 30%. If he gains 28% on the whole, then how many did he sell at a gain of 20%?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Alligation Method** to find the ratio of quantities:

Gain 1 (20%) −−− Gain 2 (30%) with Mean Gain (28%)

Ratio = (30 − 28) : (28 − 20) = 2 : 8 = 1 : 4

Total units = 1 + 4 = 5 units

5 units = 240 Televisions ⇒ 1 unit = 240 ÷ 5 = 48

**∴ The correct answer is 48.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of Televisions = 240

Gain on Part 1 = 20%

Gain on Part 2 = 30%

Overall Gain = 28%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/114a238e52f17d322684a5e072de3ca9671628ab89f78365197309c2af71dde0.png] 

Let the number of TVs sold at 20% gain be **x** and at 30% gain be **(240 − x)**.

⇒ 20x + 30(240 − x) = 28 × 240

⇒ 20x + 7200 − 30x = 6720

⇒ −10x = 6720 − 7200

⇒ −10x = −480

⇒ x = 480 ÷ 10

⇒ x = 48

**∴ The correct answer is 48.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation

It is used to find the ratio in which two ingredients at given prices/percentages must be mixed to produce a mixture of a desired price/percentage. Ratio = (Higher Value − Mean) : (Mean − Lower Value).

Weighted Average Formula

Average = (n₁v₁ + n₂v₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the quantity and v is the value (like gain % or price).

Profit Percentage

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100. When multiple items are sold, the overall profit % is the weighted average of individual profit percentages.</p

questions.question: If 20% of x = y, then y% of 20 is the same as:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the property: **a% of b = b% of a**.

Required: **y% of 20** is the same as **20% of y**.

Substitute **y = 20% of x**:

20% of (20% of x) = (20 × 20) ÷ 100 % of x = **4% of x**.

**∴ The correct answer is 4% of x.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 20% of x = y

**Formula:** a% of b = (a × b) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/97df565c5fa4e458778f1201f24b87ffb0037e4d1d2a1ed176d09434e5fc6cc5.png] 

⇒ y = (20 ÷ 100) × x

⇒ y = 0.2x

⇒ Required value = y% of 20

⇒ Required value = (y ÷ 100) × 20

⇒ Substitute y = 0.2x: ((0.2x) ÷ 100) × 20

⇒ Required value = (4x) ÷ 100

⇒ Required value = 4% of x

**∴ The correct answer is 4% of x.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Interchangeability

The property **a% of b = b% of a** is a powerful tool to simplify calculations like 16% of 50, which is the same as 50% of 16 = 8.

Successive Percentages

When one percentage is applied over another, the net percentage is **(a × b) ÷ 100 %** of the base value.

Fractional Conversions

Memorizing standard fractions (e.g., 20% = 1/5, 25% = 1/4) helps in solving percentage problems much faster during competitive exams.

questions.question: An article is sold at a 20% loss. If the selling price was ₹400 more, there would have been a 5% gain. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total percentage difference = Loss% + Gain% = 20% + 5% = 25%

This 25% difference is equal to the price increase of ₹400.

⇒ 25% of Cost Price = ₹400

⇒ 100% of Cost Price = 400 × (100 ÷ 25) = 400 × 4 = ₹1600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Loss = 20%

New Gain = 5%

Increase in Selling Price (SP) = ₹400

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (100 ± Profit/Loss%)/100

CP = (Difference in SP × 100) ÷ (Total % change)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b46b6dfbf2a4fa7011871dbf4bb13e045ad9aa749b86544ee7167d6b03f6034.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the article be ₹x.

⇒ Initial Selling Price (SP₁) = x − 20% of x = 0.80x

⇒ New Selling Price (SP₂) = x + 5% of x = 1.05x

⇒ According to the question: SP₂ − SP₁ = 400

⇒ 1.05x − 0.80x = 400

⇒ 0.25x = 400

⇒ x = 400 ÷ 0.25

⇒ x = 400 × (100 ÷ 25)

⇒ x = 400 × 4 = 1600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 and Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. Both are always calculated on the Cost Price unless stated otherwise.

Marked Price and Discount

Selling Price = Marked Price − Discount. Discount % is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP).

Successive Discounts

If two discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the effective discount = (d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100)%.

questions.question:
A wholesaler offers a 25% discount on purchases of ₹10000 or more. A customer buys goods worth ₹15000.

If he also gets an additional 5% discount for paying cash, how much does he pay?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive discount formula: Net Discount % = d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100

Net Discount = 25 + 5 − (25 × 5)/100 = 30 − 1.25 = 28.75%

Amount Paid = (100 − 28.75)% of 15000 = 71.25% of 15000

Amount Paid = 15000 × 0.7125 = 10687.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10687.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a4434c6bdd288dc440d10aad45febd98e47c349737eb745b62703f78651f1e9.png] 

**Given:**

Total purchase value = ₹15000

Wholesale discount (for ≥ ₹10000) = 25%

Additional cash discount = 5%

**Formula Used:**

Final Price = Marked Price × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since ₹15000 > ₹10000, the 25% discount applies.

⇒ Price after 25% discount = 15000 − (25/100 × 15000)

⇒ Price after 25% discount = 15000 − 3750 = ₹11250

⇒ Additional 5% cash discount is applied on the reduced price.

⇒ Cash discount = 5/100 × 11250 = ₹562.50

⇒ Final amount paid = 11250 − 562.50 = ₹10687.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10687.50.**

questions.question: 8 men can complete a work in 12 days. How many men are required to complete the same work in 6 days?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Work Equivalence** formula: M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂

Where M = **Men** and D = **Days**.

8 × 12 = M₂ × 6

96 = M₂ × 6

M₂ = 96 ÷ 6 = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Initial number of men (M₁) = 8

⇒ Initial number of days (D₁) = 12

⇒ Target number of days (D₂) = 6

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Men × Days (assuming efficiency of 1 man is 1 unit/day)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Work = M₁ × D₁ = 8 × 12 = 96 man-days

⇒ To complete 96 units of work in 6 days:

⇒ Required Men (M₂) = Total Work ÷ D₂

⇒ M₂ = 96 ÷ 6

⇒ M₂ = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

**__Additional Information__**

General Chain Rule

The relationship between men, days, hours, and work is given by (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂.

Inverse Proportion in Work

The number of men is **inversely proportional** to the time taken to complete a constant amount of work (M ∝ 1/D).

Man-Days Concept

The product of the number of workers and the time they work represents the **total volume of work**, often expressed in man-hours or man-days.</p

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 18 days. They worked together for 12 days and then B left. A finished the remaining work in 10 days. In how many days can A alone complete the work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Remaining work for (A+B) = 18 − 12 = 6 days of work.

A takes 10 days to complete this 6-day work of (A+B).

Efficiency ratio (A+B) : A = 10 : 6 = 5 : 3.

Total work = Efficiency (A+B) × Total days = 5 × 18 = 90 units.

Time taken by A alone = 90 ÷ 3 = 30 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (A+B) can do work in 18 days. They work together for 12 days. A finishes remaining work in 10 days.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Efficiency × Time

⇒ Let total work be 18 × 5 = 90 units (based on efficiency ratio).

⇒ Work done by (A+B) in 12 days = 12 × 5 = 60 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 90 − 60 = 30 units.

⇒ A's efficiency = Remaining work ÷ Time = 30 ÷ 10 = 3 units/day.

⇒ Time taken by A alone = Total work ÷ A's efficiency = 90 ÷ 3 = 30 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work. If the ratio of efficiency of A and B is x:y, then the ratio of time taken by them is y:x.

Combined Work Formula

If A can do a piece of work in 'x' days and B can do it in 'y' days, then together they can finish the work in (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed among workers in the ratio of the work done by them, which is the same as the ratio of their efficiencies if they work for the same amount of time.</p

questions.question: If a sum doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest, what is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Sum **doubles** means **Interest** earned is **100%** of the **Principal**.

**Rate of interest (R)** = **Total Interest %** ÷ **Time (T)**

**Rate** = **100%** ÷ **8** = **12.5%**

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let **Principal (P)** = 100

**Amount (A)** = 2 × 100 = 200 (since it doubles)

**Time (T)** = **8 years**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/478f88c9868abdcb1625ead0f8846d8e53438399dd499b09386ff1b461d5e512.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Simple Interest (SI)** = (**P** × **R** × **T**) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ **SI** = **Amount** − **Principal**

⇒ **SI** = 200 − 100 = 100

⇒ 100 = (100 × **R** × 8) ÷ 100

⇒ 100 = **R** × 8

⇒ **R** = 100 ÷ 8

⇒ **R** = **12.5%**

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

**SI** = (**P** × **R** × **T**) ÷ 100, where **P** is **Principal**, **R** is **Rate per annum**, and **T** is **Time in years**.

Relation for n times

If a sum becomes **n times** in **T years** at **Simple Interest**, then **R × T = (n − 1) × 100**.

Amount in Simple Interest

**Amount (A)** = **Principal (P)** + **Simple Interest (SI)** = **P**[1 + (**RT** ÷ 100)].</p

questions.question:
A sum of Rs. 427 is to be divided among X, Y and Z such that 3 times X's share, 4 times Y's share and 7 times Z's share are all equal.
The share of Z is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of X : Y : Z = (4 × 7) : (3 × 7) : (3 × 4) = 28 : 21 : 12

Total ratio units = 28 + 21 + 12 = 61 units

Total amount = Rs. 427

Value of 1 unit = 427 ÷ 61 = 7

Z's share = 12 units = 12 × 7 = 84

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 84.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total sum to be divided = Rs. 427

Condition: 3 × X = 4 × Y = 7 × Z

**Formula Used:**

If aX = bY = cZ, then X : Y : Z = (1/a) : (1/b) : (1/c)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ad232715adf235fda018b7aba87b61717e082ca5d85c42e73e36518f3304156c.png] 

⇒ Let 3X = 4Y = 7Z = k

⇒ X = k/3, Y = k/4, Z = k/7

⇒ Ratio of X : Y : Z = 1/3 : 1/4 : 1/7

⇒ LCM of 3, 4, and 7 is 84

⇒ X : Y : Z = (1/3 × 84) : (1/4 × 84) : (1/7 × 84)

⇒ X : Y : Z = 28 : 21 : 12

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 28 + 21 + 12 = 61

⇒ Z's share = (Z's ratio part ÷ Total ratio parts) × Total Sum

⇒ Z's share = (12 ÷ 61) × 427

⇒ Z's share = 12 × 7 = 84

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 84.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Ratio Property

If aX = bY, then the ratio X : Y is the inverse of their coefficients, i.e., X : Y = b : a.

Ratio Normalization

To convert a fractional ratio like 1/a : 1/b : 1/c into a whole number ratio, multiply each term by the LCM of (a, b, c).

Proportional Distribution

The share of any individual in a total sum S divided in ratio a:b:c is calculated as [a/(a+b+c)] × S.</p

questions.question: A semi circular window has a diameter of 1.4 meters. What is the total length of the frame required for this window?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Perimeter of a semi-circle = r(π + 2) = r(36/7)

Given: Diameter = 1.4 m ⇒ Radius (r) = 0.7 m

Perimeter = 0.7 × (36/7) = 0.1 × 36 = 3.6 m

**∴ The correct answer is 3.6 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of the semi-circular window (d) = 1.4 m

**Formula Used:**

Total length of frame = Circumference of semi-circle + Diameter

Total length = πr + d

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bb575cf8feac9dd9b38fda4cee8f7afbb183312a1568be04ba68b8128cb4da57.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Radius (r) = Diameter ÷ 2 = 1.4 ÷ 2 = 0.7 m

⇒ Length of the curved arc = π × r

⇒ Arc length = (22/7) × 0.7 = 2.2 m

⇒ Total length of the frame = Arc length + Diameter

⇒ Total length = 2.2 + 1.4 = 3.6 m

**∴ The correct answer is 3.6 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Semi-circle

The area enclosed by a semi-circle is half the area of a full circle: Area = 1/2 × πr².

Perimeter of a Quadrant

For a quarter circle, the perimeter includes the arc and two radii: Perimeter = (πr/2) + 2r.

Circumference of a Full Circle

The total boundary length of a complete circle is given by: C = 2 × π × r or π × d.

questions.question: Two cars start from the same point. One travels north at 60 km/h, the other travels east at 80 km/h. What is the distance between them after 2 hours?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

North and East directions are perpendicular (90°).

Identify the speed ratio: 60 km/h : 80 km/h → 3 : 4.

Using the Pythagorean triplet (3, 4, 5), the resultant speed ratio is 5.

Relative speed between them = 20 × 5 = 100 km/h.

Distance after 2 hours = 100 km/h × 2 hours = 200 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 200 km.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Speed of Car 1 (North) = 60 km/h

Speed of Car 2 (East) = 80 km/h

Time = 2 hours

Formula Used: Distance = Speed × Time | Pythagoras Theorem: c² = a² + b²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5173efd5fab812b2908713d54b41bd27f2e61bdf49473933cc4eca89d8e3c4ab.png] 

Calculations:

⇒ Distance traveled North = 60 × 2 = 120 km

⇒ Distance traveled East = 80 × 2 = 160 km

⇒ Total Distance (D) = √((120)² + (160)²)

⇒ D = √(14400 + 25600)

⇒ D = √40000

⇒ D = 200 km

**∴ The correct answer is 200 km.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Triplets

Common sets of integers that satisfy a² + b² = c² include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17). Any multiple of these is also a triplet.

Direction Relations

Cardinal directions (North, South, East, West) are always at 90° to their adjacent directions, allowing the use of right-angle geometry.

Resultant Speed

If two objects move perpendicularly with speeds v₁ and v₂, the speed of separation is √(v₁² + v₂²).</p

questions.question: A cone has a base radius of 7 cm and height of 24 cm. What is its slant height?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a cone, the radius (r), height (h), and slant height (l) form a right-angled triangle.

Apply the Pythagorean triplet (7, 24, 25).

Since the base radius is 7 cm and the height is 24 cm, the slant height must be 25 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius (r) = 7 cm

Height (h) = 24 cm

**Formula Used:**

Slant height (l) = √(r² + h²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a235a9c79c0d785d637547eea1096d1af8b1ce9a00c5abdcf244cf006ef1f15b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ l = √(7² + 24²)

⇒ l = √(49 + 576)

⇒ l = √625

⇒ l = 25 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 25 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area of a Cone

The lateral surface area is calculated as CSA = π × r × l, where r is radius and l is slant height.

Total Surface Area of a Cone

The sum of the curved area and the base area: TSA = π × r × (l + r).

Volume of a Cone

The volume of a cone is one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same radius and height: V = (1/3) × π × r² × h.

Pythagorean Triplets

A Pythagorean triplet consists of three positive integers a, b, and c, such that a² + b² = c². Examples: (3, 4, 5), (8, 15, 17), (7, 24, 25).</p

questions.question: A triangle has two angles measuring 65° and 45°. What is the measure of the third angle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Angle Sum Property: Total internal angle of a triangle = 180°.

Third angle = 180° − (Sum of known angles)

Third angle = 180° − (65° + 45°) = 180° − 110° = 70°.

**∴ The correct answer is 70°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First angle (∠A) = 65°

Second angle (∠B) = 45°

**Formula Used:**

Sum of angles in a triangle = ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9f3eebe293ea4b6d4f857c7651760cb6e62f2be0e730293855ca303c9993f8f0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the third angle be x.

⇒ 65° + 45° + x = 180°

⇒ 110° + x = 180°

⇒ x = 180° − 110°

⇒ x = 70°

**∴ The correct answer is 70°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Types of Triangles by Angles

Acute: All angles 90°.

Exterior Angle Property

The exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of its two interior opposite angles.

Polygon Angle Sum Formula

The sum of interior angles of any polygon with n sides is given by (n − 2) × 180°.
